hook: SCP-1485 is a doorway into a parallel world almost identical to ours, apart from one difference. The containment procedures look strange at first, guarding the portal mainly against the Foundation's own staff; the liaison log and closing interview explain why.
whyItMatters: A defense grid built for a possible invasion has been turned around to stop unauthorized people from going in, and that reversal sums up the article's real concern. The danger is not what might come through but who might choose not to come back. The interview gets its force from an agent describing plain everyday life as something she had been missing.
thingsToNotice: SCP-1485-A has no anomalies, no Foundation equivalent and no Groups of Interest, and anyone trying to contain the paranormal there is laughed at. Desertions grow from two agents to an entire ten-person liaison team, of whom only two are caught: one kills themselves before capture and the other turns themselves in to the local authorities. That agent, a trusted nine-year veteran, describes feeling a great weight lifted and explains her defection with no grand motive, only that over there your eyes, your senses and science can all be trusted because nothing hides at the edge of sight. Her final answer is simply that the world makes sense. Meanwhile the other side has grown hostile, calling our universe a threat and pressing to seal the portal for good.
